Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. West Triangle, Quezon City http: ltwww. dilg.gov.ph DIR. JAMES F. FADRILAN, CESC) 111 Regional Director DILG Regional Office 1 Aguila Road, Sevilla Norte, City of San Fernando, La Union, 2500 Dear Dir. Fadrilan: on-G OPINION NO. 0 1 JUN 2018 This has reference to your letter dated 29 January 2018 requesting this level's opinion on the query of Mr. Gigender Ram, Owner-operator of Derille's Enterprises and D&G PDD Farm relative to the imposition of Livestock Quarantine Regulatory Fees under the Provincial Tax Ordinance No. 001-2008 of the Province of La Union on the transport of frozen goods, poultry products and dressed chicken into and out of Province of La Union, and whether it is contrary to the provisions of the Local Government Code (LGC) and DILG Memorandum Circulars. Foremost, per your letter, the herein imposition of Livestock Quarantine Regulatory Fees is provided under the Provincial Tax Ordinance No. 001-2008. Therefore, this level is inclined to presume that the purpose of this imposition is clearly for revenue purposes. It must be noted that there are three inherent powers of the state delegated to the Local Government Units (LGUs). These are the Police Power, Power of Eminent Domain, and Power of Taxation. In the case of Planters Product, Inc., vs. Fertphil Corporationl, the Supreme Court discussed the difference between the Police Power and Power of Taxation, thus: "Police power and the power Of taxation are inherent powers of the State. These powers are distinct and have different tests for validity. Police power is the power of the State to enact legislation that may interfere with personal liberty_ or property in order to promote the general welfare. while the weroftaxationis the wertol taxes to be for ubli . The main purpose efpolicepvwer is the regulation ofa behavior or. conduct. while tpxation is revenue generation. The lawful subjects and lawful means tests are G.R. No. 166006, March 14, 2008

used to determine the validity ofa law enacted under the police power. The power of taxation, on the other hand, is circumscribed by inherent and constitutional limitations. We agree with the RTC that the imposition of the levy was an exercise by the State of its taxation power. While it is true that the power of taxation can be used as an implement of police power. the primary purpose of the levy is revenue generation. If the purpose is primarily revenue: or if revenue is. at es then the ctio i ro rl least one of the real and ubstantial called a tax. " em hasis ours Therefore, it is this level's view that the herein questioned fee is an exercise of the power of taxation and used to implement the police power because of the following reasons: 1. The said imposition was provided in the Provincial Tax Ordinance No. OOI- 2008, therefore the LGUs intention is for revenue purposes; 2. It runs contrast with what is provided in the letter dated 21 December 2017 from Governor Ortega that the imposition of the same is actually to prevent animal disease into and out of La Union, and the taxes collected as a result thereof is merely secondary as the same is an invocation of the police power of the state. How can it be secondary if the same is provided in the tax ordinance which the primary purpose for its passage is for revenue? Moreover, the herein Provincial Tax Ordinance was crafted in 2008, while in the letter of Governor Ortega, the justification Of this imposition was due to the occurrence of the avian flu outbreak in Nueva Ecija and Pampanga which occurred in 2017 only. Please note that Section 489 (b)(3) did not provide for collection of any amount of money for regulation thereof. "SECTION489. Qualifications, Powers and Duties. xxx (3) In addition to the foregoing duties and functions, the veterinarian shall: (i) Advise the governor or the mayor, as the case may be, on all matters pertaining to the slaughter of animals for human consumption and the regulation of slaughterhouses; (ii) Regulate the keeping ofdomestic animals; (iii) Regulate and inspect poultry, milk and dairy products Tor public consumption; (iv) Enforce all laws and regulations for the prevention of cruelty to animals; and

(v) Take the necessary measures to eradicate, prevent or cure all forms Of animal diseases; " The taxing power of the LGU is not all encompassing as it has certain limitations. Relative to this, may we invite you to the pertinent provision of the LGC which provides: SECTION 133. Common Limitations on the Taxing Powers of Local Government Units. - Unless otherwise provided herein, the exercise of the taxingpowers of provinces, cities, municipalities, and barangays shall not extend to the levy of the following: (e) Taxes, fees, and charges and other impositions upon goods carried into or out of, or passing through, the territorial jurisdictions of local government units in the guise of charges for wharfage, tolls for bridges or otherwise, or other taxes, fees, or charges in any form whatsoever upon such goods or merchandise; Wherefore, it is this level's view that the herein imposition of Livestock Quarantine Regulatory Fees on the transport of frozen goods, poultry products and dressed chicken into and out of Province of La Union, is prohibited as it is within the limitation of the taxing powers of an LGU. Nevertheless, it is this level's opinion that the LGU, through the provincial veterinarian can regulate the same without collecting certain amount in the guise of tax and other fees, or the said imposition be included during the issuance of business permits. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHOR F THE SECRETARY: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecre LIW37
